summary: # 【Marvelous Designer X Crytek】Learning Day Special Guest Juefei p02 Sherry ## Introduction In today's session, Juefei shares insights into working with Marvelous Designer (MD) and the various techniques used in creating digital fabric simulations. The discussion covers the process of designing elements like bed boards, cushions, and quilts while addressing common challenges and tips for optimization. --- ## Creating a Bed Board When I create a bed board or similar items, I start by drawing a hard board on paper. Then, I modify its dimensions and thickness to complete the construction. Essentially, I’m taking a lazy approach. After adding the thickness, the board will have a defined depth. ### Adjusting Features I often find that the corners are too rounded, so I might reduce the edge curve. By adjusting the thickness, I can modify the board as desired. Once I finish with the thickness, I draw the inner lines and cut the boards according to my specifications. ### Using 3D Software These steps can be performed in various 3D software, but I usually stick with AMD and don’t explore others. There are different methods to achieve the same result. This is how the board gets completed. By varying the thickness, we can create an old-fashioned wooden bed board. --- ## Further Adjustments After making the initial adjustments to the edge, I position another board on top to match a star pattern. Once I finish the bed board, I think about the next steps. *“Oh, I'm ugly! I'm ugly! This is what you call being ugly.”* --- ## Inner Lines and Effects I will draw some inner lines to create a specific effect. Marvelous Designer (MD) allows for a wide range of designs. After drawing the inner lines, I adjust their position slightly. ### Inspiration from Others I recall someone named Zhang Yu using MD to create unique items like umbrellas. Based on the feedback I received, it seems a glove tutorial might be in demand for the next live stream. ### Pressure and Tension When I apply pressure, it generates a certain effect. The next live stream will cover a new feature, likely around Christmas. I plan to reduce the particle diameter for the created version, as certain wrinkles become invisible at a diameter of 20. --- ## Pressure and Thickness Applying pressure changes the resulting appearance, especially after reducing the particle diameter. The created version will have a pronounced "pung-pung" effect. I have contemplated making high-end designs, but I find it easier to use other 3D graphics tools. ### Rendering Adjustments I continue adjusting the rendering thickness. I noticed a gap in the middle, prompting further adjustments. I found that turning off the border curve resulted in some long ends. By enabling it again, I can make the necessary corrections. --- ## Exporting the Model I will export the bed sheet as an OBJ file. Initially, I wanted to write everything in English, but I ended up using Pinyin due to memory issues. When exporting, I prefer to do it as multiple goals for easier texture adjustments later. ### Understanding Collisions In MD, the collision between boards is crucial for proper simulation. If we want the bed to interact with other objects, we must export and re-import the model in a virtual format after finishing in MD. ### Exploring Other Designs I’ve previously created various items in MD, including necklaces. I recall a competition where someone showcased their skills using MD, impressing me with their work. --- ## Common Challenges At times, I feel overwhelmed, especially when the computer lags during recording. I activate models and create versions to alleviate this. I often compress the video speed to save time, drawing versions to lay on the bed. ### Creating a Quilt I aim to create a bed sheet that wraps around the bed, which involves manual adjustments. I often think about what to do while recording the video, adding elements piece by piece. ### Flexibility in Design For mattresses, I aim for flexibility. This allows the design to fold and shrink naturally. I adjust the model as needed, ensuring it fits snugly. --- ## Finalizing the Design Once the bed sheet is complete, I look at reference images to inform my next steps. I draw internal lines to ensure the design translates well into simulation. The folding arrangement tools are crucial for achieving the desired look. ### Simulation Techniques I often simulate smaller sections to avoid lag, progressively building up to larger designs. This technique helps streamline the creation process and ensures the final product meets expectations. --- ## Community Interaction As I wrap up, I encourage viewers to ask questions, especially regarding MD and 3D design. I emphasize that all software has its strengths and should complement each other in production. ### Conclusion I appreciate everyone’s attention during this session. For further inquiries, viewers can leave comments, and I will respond as best as I can. Thank you for joining, and I look forward to our next session! --- *Note: This document is a structured representation of the original transcript, maintained for accuracy and coherence.
